Need to search first.I couldn't write these notes, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

**What went wrong:**
1. I first tried to open six pages directly: the Enduring Word commentary on Isaiah 65, the Ellicott, Pulpit and Gill commentaries on biblehub.com, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. All six failed. The tool only opens addresses that have already come up in a search, and I hadn't run one yet.
2. I then ran the searches that should have found those pages, along with pages on the main debates (Isaiah 65:20 and the millennium, Paul's use of v. 1 in Romans 10:20, and readings of v. 17 and v. 25). By then I had used up my allowance of tool calls for this turn, so nothing came back.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to leave out what I couldn't find. Since I read no pages, writing verse notes would mean using my own memory and attaching web addresses I haven't checked. I haven't done that.

**Next step:** if you send the request again (just "continue" should do it), I'll start fresh in this order:
1. Search for the verse-by-verse commentaries (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Pulpit, Gill, Precept Austin, NET Bible notes) and read them.
2. Look for pages where the traditions differ, especially on vv. 17–25: whether the passage describes a future thousand-year reign, the new creation, or the church today.
3. Look at the Catholic and Orthodox sites and the modern scholarship sites, but only where they discuss this chapter.

Then I'll write the notes verse by verse with a web address for each point, and leave out any verse I can't find sources for.
